segments.en: And this is the aspect of the wine of the Four Cups. For wine contains two aspects — as our Sages said (Yoma 76b): "If he merits — it makes him a head [rosh]; if he does not merit — it makes him a pauper [rash]." That is, when one merits, the da'as is elevated through the wine — and the essential da'as is the revelation of hashgachah. That is, the da'as of hashgachah is revealed even more through the drinking of wine, when one merits — the aspect of: "if he merits, he becomes a head." But if he does not merit, it is the opposite — for "he becomes a pauper" — and there is no poverty except from da'as. And from there is the essential poverty in actuality — that is, when one lacks the da'as of hashgachah, which is the essential da'as — from there comes poverty — the aspect of: "in sorrow you shall eat of it" (Genesis 3:17) — which is the aspect of hardship and poverty that comes through the blemish of eating of the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil — which is the aspect of the wisdom of nature, as above. For nature is the aspect of darkness and night, the aspect of the blemish of the moon, as above — from which is the essential poverty, as is known. And these two aspects are encompassed in wine — for wine brings sleep — and this is the aspect of nature, which is the aspect of night and sleep, as above. And conversely, when one merits, the wine awakens from sleep — in the aspect of: "and your palate is like good wine — moving the lips of those who sleep" (Song of Songs 7:10). That is, the good wine, from the side of good, awakens from sleep — which is the aspect of speech. For during sleep, speech departs — and through the good wine, one is awakened from sleep and speech is drawn, which comes from the da'as, as is known — the aspect of: "moving the lips of those who sleep." And this is the aspect of hashgachah, which is the aspect of awakening from sleep, as above. And because wine is encompassed of the two aspects — the aspect of da'as, the aspect of hashgachah — which is the aspect of joyful wine, the aspect of alma d'asei — the aspect of: "and wine that gladdens" (Psalms 104:15) — etc. — and this is when one merits, as above. And if he does not merit, it is the aspect of intoxicating wine, which confuses the da'as and errs in the wisdom of nature, G-d forbid — which is the aspect of sleep, etc. — as above. Therefore, one must guard the wine very much from the touch of idolaters — more than anything else in the world. For nothing else becomes forbidden through the touch of an idolater — only wine becomes nesech [libation] through the touch of an idolater. For as soon as the idolater touches the wine — and ordinary touching is with the hands — then the wine is drawn to the aspect of nature — which is the aspect of the idolatrous nations of the world. Because the wine is encompassed of the two aspects, as above — therefore, the idolaters — who are the aspect of nature — can defile the wine through their touch with their hand — for it is immediately drawn to the aspect of nature. And therefore, it is not fit for Israel — who are above nature — and all their foods and beverages must be holy — that through the food and drink the da'as of hashgachah should be drawn, as above. And therefore, the essential blemish of the wine is through their touch — and ordinary touch is with the hands — for the essential blemish of the da'as of hashgachah is through the blemish of the hands — the blemish of the 28 joints of the hands, which correspond to the 28 letters of the account of Creation, etc. — as above. And the hands of the idolaters are the opposite of this — and they are in the aspect of: "the hands are the hands of Eisav" (Genesis 27:22) — the aspect of the error of nature — which is the aspect of: "my power and the might of my hand," as above. And therefore, the wine is blemished through the idolaters, as above — and then it becomes nesech. This is the aspect of the error of the wisdom of nature — which is the aspect of sleep. And this is the aspect of nesech — the aspect of: "for Hashem has poured [nasach] upon you a spirit of deep sleep" (Isaiah 29:10) — etc. — which is said there regarding the stargazers who err in the arrangement of the heavens, as above. And therefore, at the time of the redemption from Egypt — when the hashgachah was revealed — then it is a mitzvah to drink four cups of wine. For then the wine is in the aspect of: "if he merits, he becomes a head." For now, on the night of Pesach, the da'as is elevated and the hashgachah is revealed even more through the wine. For Hashem yisbarach drew hashgachah and broke the night and sleep — in the aspect of: "At about midnight, I will go out in the midst of Egypt" (Exodus 11:4). And then the wine is the aspect of joyful wine — and one can speak and tell of the Exodus from Egypt on this night through the wine — in the aspect of: "moving the lips of those who sleep," as above. And this is the aspect of (Berachos 35a): "Song is said only over wine." For all the songs are drawn from the aspect of alma d'asei, where song shall be aroused in the world — as is written in the Holy Zohar — in the aspect of: "Then Moshe will sing" — "sang" is not stated, rather "will sing" — from here [we learn] that he is destined to sing in the World to Come. For the essential song is from the aspect of the World to Come, where Moshe will sing, etc. — for then, song shall be aroused in the world. And from there, all the songs are drawn to this world — that we sing and chant regarding the miracles. For all the miracles are performed through Hashem yisbarach drawing the aspect of hashgachah from the ends of the world — from the World to Come — to this world, as above. And then, when the miracle is performed, we also draw the aspect of song from the World to Come to this world. And this is the aspect of all the songs of the miracles. And therefore, "song is said only over wine" — for then the wine is encompassed in holiness, in the aspect of the da'as of hashgachah. And this is the essential aspect of the song — that one draws the aspect of hashgachah — which is the aspect of the song of the miracle — to this world. And therefore, one says the song over wine, as above. And this is the aspect of the four cups of wine of Pesach — corresponding to the four kingdoms. For when the wine is encompassed in holiness, in the aspect of hashgachah — through this, all the exiles of all the four kingdoms are subdued — whose essential power is through nature, as above. And through the hashgachah that is revealed through the da'as that is drawn through the cups of wine — through this, they are all nullified, etc. — as above.
